text.p: Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci), whose bank Banamex is obliged to raise some four billion pesos in new capital this year, will keep share dilution to a bare minimum, a top bank official said.
"We are going to minimize dilution," Jorge Hierro, deputy director general of Banacci, said in an interview. "We have never said never (to dilution), but look at our track record."

The banking group, whose banking unit is Mexico's largest, pledged to raise the capital after selling eight billion pesos of past-due loans, net of reserves, to the government's Bank Insurance Fund (Fobaproa) in late December.
Banacci prided itself last year on raising more than double that amount of capital with no immediate increase in the number of shares, a feat it said distinguished it from its rivals.
But analysts, some who were already agog at its juggling feat to avoid a rights issue last year, now wonder where it can find yet more capital without hurting shareholders.

"We have a menu of options," Hierro said cagily, maintaining a Banacci policy of keeping its capitalization plans well up its sleeve. "What I can say is that an equity issue is the most distant possibility."

He played down one long-standing rumor that has resurfaced since Banamex announced its capitalization obligations last week: The possibility that Banacci could sell a stake in its prestigious brokerage Accival to a U.S. suitor.

"We imagine that the sale of Accival (or part of it) is a likely possibility to increase the bank's equity. There have been rumors for a long time that a well known U.S. investment bank has reached an agreement to buy a stake," Bear Stearns banking analyst Alberto Sanchez wrote in a report this week.
Other analysts said Goldman, Sachs and Co or Merrill Lynch and Co Inc may be the two most interested potential partners.
But Hierro said the rumor was old and no deal was even close. "Ideas on alliances emerge all the time. I would say it would be very premature (to speculate)," he added.
He noted that some $125 million of the $500 million the bank intends to raise is already in its pocket; he said that came from excess capital among its international subsidiaries.

Last year, Banacci raised around $1 billion in capital by fusing its leasing, factoring, and foreign exchange units with Banamex, issuing $350 million of subordinated exchangeable debentures and revaluing joint ventures.
